decisions.reason: Although it targets sports use, it builds on the firm's existing flooring-system know-how and in-house R&D gives management enough absorptive capacity to improve it rather than exit quickly.

The mobile arena floor is related to the firm's capabilities but is a more specialized and less style-aligned system product, so management is relatively likely to reallocate resources if learning and scale remain limited.

As another mobile arena floor close to B, it is more exposed to portfolio rationalization because the firm can learn from the segment but may judge the niche too narrow versus its core development path.
This chevron hardwood parquet is very close to the firm's core residential design-led offer, so existing knowledge and R&D make it highly likely that management keeps and refines it.
A squash-court surface finish fits the firm's wood-surface expertise and benefits from related technical knowledge, making continued commercialization more likely than withdrawal.
Oak skirting for sports floors is a complementary add-on that draws directly on the firm's material and finishing capabilities, so it is relatively cheap to support and likely to be retained.
